model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the perceived importance of various measures that could potentially limit the "shadow economy" within a country. The horizontal axis displays a list of fifteen measures, including "To strengthen customs control," "To limit the actions of the mafia," "To facilitate access to credit," "To reduce corruption," "To improve the quality of administrative services," "To increase the effectiveness of the judicial system," "To strengthen tax control," "To introduce more effective incentives for business," "To adopt stricter laws," "To reduce taxes," "To reduce VAT," "To reduce profit tax," and "To reduce personal income tax." The vertical axis is labeled with a percentage scale ranging from 0% to 15%, with tick labels at 0%, 2%, 4%, 6%, 8%, 10%, 12%, and 14%. Each measure is represented by a single horizontal bar, with varying lengths corresponding to the percentage value. The bars are colored in shades of blue and gray. The shortest bars, representing "To strengthen customs control," "To reduce taxes," and "To reduce personal income tax," have a length of approximately 2%. The tallest bar, representing "To improve the quality of administrative services," has a length of approximately 13%. The bars are sorted in descending order based on their corresponding percentage values, with the longest bars appearing first. No bars are visually emphasized beyond their color and length.
